newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Oil to raise $1.0 bln loan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Indian Oil to raise $1.0 bln loan - paper.

text.p: The state-run Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) has contracted a fully underwritten two-tranche $1.0 billion one-year syndicated loan facility to fund oil imports in 1997/98 (April-March), the Financial Express newspaper said on Friday.
"The first tranche of $500 million, inclusive of a $100 million greenshoe option, has been fully contracted at an all-in cost of 25.5 basis points over LIBOR," the paper said.
ABN AMRO Bank will be the coordinating arranger along with Kredietbank NV and Dresdner South-east Asia Ltd, it said.
"The structured finance obligation for IOC will soon be sold down to other banks, primarily in the Asian region," it said.
Indian Oil officials were not immediately available for comment.
Indian Oil has a monopoly over crude oil imports and is the main importer of major petroleum products.
